source: Self-Improving AI Agent Reflection Loops (Analytics Vidhya, 2026)
summary: Survey of generate→critique→revise reflection patterns for agents; ReAct, Reflexion, Self-Refine lineage. Verbal self-reflection boosts HumanEval pass@1 from 80% to 91%.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already implements a review→address loop (AddressingReview state); adversarial critique pre-approval is tracked in HID-93; partial retry in HID-186.

summary: Karpathy presented agentic engineering at Sequoia Ascent 2026: spec design, diff review, eval loops, maintaining conceptual ownership. Distinguishes vibe coding from principled agentic engineering.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — principles align with AgentForge's state machine design; skill distillation and planner injection already shipped (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). The LLM wiki/knowledge compounding pattern could extend distillation but executor prompts not receiving skills yet is tracked implicitly under HID-188.

summary: LangChain and LangGraph reached v1.0 with LangMem agent memory library; LangGraph 1.2.6 ships built-in cross-session memory stores, MongoDB and Oracle integrations, middleware layer.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is TypeScript/Fastify, not Python/LangChain. Cross-session memory concept is tracked in HID-188.

source: Vestige: Local-First Cognitive Memory MCP Server (github.com/samvallad33/vestige)
summary: Rust-based MCP server providing FSRS-6 spaced-repetition decay, spreading activation, contradiction detection, and 3D memory dashboard for MCP-compatible coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge uses its own skill distillation pipeline (distillationAgent.ts) rather than MCP-based memory. Cross-run episodic memory is tracked in HID-188. The FSRS-6 decay/forgetting mechanics are interesting but out of scope for AgentForge's architecture.

summary: CrewAI 1.14 removed LangChain dependency, added A2A protocol support, MCP tool integration, and streaming. Better vector-based cross-session memory announced for Q1 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses, not API-based agent frameworks. A2A protocol is not applicable to AgentForge's architecture.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (AutoGen + Semantic Kernel merger, April 2026)
summary: Microsoft merged AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into Agent Framework 1.0 GA (April 2026) for .NET and Python. Adds graph-based multi-agent workflows, typed pipelines, MCP and A2A support, session-based state management, and telemetry.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — .NET/Python target; AgentForge is TypeScript/Node. The graph-based workflow and typed pipeline concept is analogous to AgentForge's stateMachine.ts but offers no adoptable patterns at this time.

source: Code as Agent Harness paper (arXiv:2605.18747, May 2026)
summary: Survey of 42 researchers arguing code as operational substrate (not just output) for agent reasoning, action, and verification. Introduces Plan-Execute-Verify (PEV) pattern with structured parsers and feedback-driven control.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — PEV pattern maps directly to AgentForge's Planning→Implementing→AIReview flow. Structured parsers and execution-based verification before implementation is tracked in HID-135 (synthesize acceptance-test harness from approved plan).

source: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI paper (arXiv:2607.07663, July 2026)
summary: Theoretical paper covering bounded self-refinement to autonomous research loops; investigates how agents can recursively improve their own architecture and training from execution traces.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Too speculative for AgentForge's practical roadmap. The recursive training loop aspect requires ML infrastructure AgentForge doesn't have. Skill distillation is the closest shipped analog.

summary: Open-source repo running a Supervisor→Executor→Reviewer loop over a codebase as a state machine; deterministic orchestration of AI agents for repeatable software execution workflows.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Architecturally very similar to AgentForge's own state machine. Primarily a comparison point. Key difference: Ferrus doesn't have Linear integration, plan approval gates, or skill distillation. No new capability gap identified versus current backlog.

summary: TypeScript-native agent runtime where a coordinator turns a goal into a task DAG with deterministic scheduling, approvals, traces, evaluation, checkpoints, and resume support.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — TypeScript-native and architecturally similar to AgentForge; the checkpoint+resume pattern is interesting but AgentForge's RESET_TO_TODO design is a deliberate simplicity choice. No new verified gap not already tracked.
